artworks.title: The Centaur Eurytion Carrying Off a Lapith Woman
artworks.description: Print after the Centauromachy type: Eurytion, wine-maddened at Peirithous' wedding, seizes a Lapith bride — the outrage that opens the battle of Lapiths and Centaurs. The named Thessalian centaur becomes the emblem of the feast gone violent.

artworks.title: West Pediment of the Temple of Zeus at Olympia (Centauromachy)
artworks.description: The Olympia west pediment stages the Lapith wedding brawl under Apollo's calm gaze. Ancient and modern viewers identify the central centaur assaulting the bride with Eurytion — the guest who broke xenia and started the Centauromachy in stone.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid's Centauromachy (as Eurytus/Eurytion) retells the drunken seizure at Peirithous' feast — the Thessalian centaur as first offender of the Lapith wedding.

popCulture.title: Eurytion
popCulture.description: Thessalian centaur of Peirithous' wedding — distinct from the Phthian king and from Geryon's herdsman of the same name.
